subject: Service continuity matrix & rehearsal schedule - RTO/RPO clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Turner <m.turner@silverline.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Operations SRE <operations@silverline.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Service continuity matrix and a couple of clarifications

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the continuity package you sent earlier. Two areas Silverline is particularly sensitive about for our RFP: (1) end-user impact during cross-region failover for low-latency inference endpoints, and (2) how long state (KV/cache) takes to rehydrate after a switchover. Our internal SREs have run simple load tests and see substantial tail‑latency blips when the KV cache is cold.

Can you confirm the following:
- Measured RTO for a full regional switchover (control plane + model rehydration) for a production chat endpoint serving 100 qps with a 4k context model.
- Expected RPO (token loss) assumptions for async replication vs warm standby.
- Do you offer any snapshot-and-restore of KV cache to shorten the warmup window? If so, what are the typical snapshot sizes and restore times for our class of models?

We referenced the high-level matrix in the RFP but need numbers to include in our SLA comparison spreadsheet. Attaching our internal acceptance criteria and a short excerpt of our runbook.

Appreciate a quick turn — Silverline would like internal approval this week to proceed to the demo/rehearsal stage.

Thanks,
Michael Turner
Head of Platform Reliability
Silverline Financial
Attachments: silverline_acceptance_criteria.pdf (doc), internal_rehearsal_checklist.xlsx (sheet)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@silverline.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service continuity matrix and a couple of clarifications

Michael — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- Measured RTO (full regional failover) for the configuration you described: typical 3–7 minutes to resume accepting steady traffic with prioritized endpoints in warm-standby mode; 10–20 minutes for full KV cache rehydration if relying on cold rebuilds.
- RPO: with async cross-region replication we recommend planning for up to 60 seconds of token loss under high QPS; with warm-standby + continuous checkpointing we can target RPO < 5s for prioritized customers.
- Snapshot/restore: yes — we provide scheduled KV snapshotting. Typical snapshot sizes vary by model and workspace: for a 4k context chat model serving 100 qps with per-tenant prefixes we estimate 400–800MB snapshot sizes; restore (restore + initial prioritized hydration) for critical prefixes ~2–6 minutes depending on network and replica locality. Full cache rehydration is workload dependent (10–20m).

A few important implementation notes:
- We maintain a hot standby control plane and model replicas in a secondary region for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers get prioritized warm pools per contract.
- For ultra-low-RTO commitments we use a combination of: (a) model weight pre-loading on GPUs, (b) persistent KV snapshot store (S3-backed checkpoints), and (c) prioritized background replay to hydrate top N prefixes first.
- Cold-start latency for model load (quantized 13B-class model) is ~30–90s depending on GPU local SSD and whether we can reuse a warmed VM image.

Action items I propose:
1) We share our DR continuity matrix (attached) with the revision that calls out prioritized snapshotting for Silverline critical endpoints.
2) Schedule a 90-minute rehearsal with your SREs next week; we’ll include a controlled failover and measure RTO/RPO and cache warmup times for three representative endpoints.
3) Prio: confirm the list of critical endpoint paths (we will only prioritize top ~50 prefixes due to memory/cost tradeoffs).

I’m attaching our DR matrix and a short PDF with the KV cache warmup methodology. Priyom from Applied ML is copied with some technical commentary below. Ben, looping you for the procurement/SLA note.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DR_Continuity_Matrix.xlsx, KV_Cache_Warmup_Estimates.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@silverline.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service continuity matrix and a couple of clarifications

Michael — adding technical detail on the cache and model warmup side. A few things to consider when you review acceptance criteria:

- What we call "KV cache": combination of short-term conversational state (per-conversation prefix keys) and long-lived token-level heuristics cached per workspace. Persistence strategy: periodic checkpoint (delta snapshots) to object storage + continuous streaming of high-frequency prefixes to a fast key-value staging tier.
- Snapshot sizes: for a 4k context chat model and a medium enterprise workspace (50k active prefixes/day) delta snapshots are usually 300–900MB; full snapshots can be multiple GBs.
- Restore behavior: we always restore control plane and model weights first. Then prioritized prefixes (top N by recent usage) are hydrated via snapshot restore + targeted replay of recent tokens from durable storage (if requested). That targeted pathway is what gets critical endpoints to sub-6-minute availability in our tests.
- Cost/ops tradeoff: Keeping additional warm workers (GPU memory reserved with model weights pre-loaded, but idle) reduces RTO dramatically (~<120s) but increases reserved capacity cost.

If Silverline needs RTO < 5 minutes at a predictable price, we should model a dedicated warm standby pool plus snapshot replication cadence of <=60s and a prioritized hydration list. I can prepare estimated cost deltas for that configuration.

—Priyom
Applied ML — Inference Systems
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aisha and Priyom — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our platform team:

- Silverline’s procurement needs a written SLA clause we can propose that describes a guaranteed RTO for our critical endpoints (goal: <=5 minutes to acceptance of traffic with prioritized prefixes hydrated). Can Redwood provide suggested SLA language including the exceptions/credits framework?
- We’ll want a copy of the rehearsal runbook and confirmation of what evidence (metrics/logs) you’ll provide after the drill (token-level traces, control-plane events, ambient QPS, and cache hit/miss over time).
- Can you also confirm whether the snapshot mechanism encrypts at rest and in transit, and whether keys can be customer-managed (KMS)?

If you can respond with the SLA paragraph and runbook link by EOD Tuesday we’ll be able to include it in the procurement packet.

Michael

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@silverline.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service continuity matrix and a couple of clarifications

Michael — appreciate the clear asks. Proposed pragmatic path forward that balances cost and the <=5 minute target:

1) SLA language (draft): "Redwood will maintain a warm-standby failover configuration for the Customer's prioritized endpoints that, in the event of a regional failure, will accept validated traffic for prioritized endpoints within 5 minutes of failover initiation, subject to the Customer providing a list of prioritized prefixes and a successful pre-failover synchronization. Exceptions include force majeure events, customer-side network inaccessibility, and any third-party outage beyond Redwood's contractual control. In the event Redwood fails to meet the guaranteed RTO for prioritized endpoints, Customer will be eligible for service credits as defined in Appendix C (credits scale with duration of degraded acceptance and number of missed prioritized endpoints)."

2) Evidence delivered post-rehearsal: full orchestration timeline (control-plane events with timestamps), sampling of per-endpoint token traces, cache hit/miss graphs, model load times, and a rehearsal summary document with identified remediation items.

3) Security: snapshots are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest with AES-256; customer-managed keys via supported KMS are available for Dedicated and Private deployments.

4) Rehearsal scheduling: propose Thu 29 Apr 2026 09:00–10:30 PT as an initial rehearsal window. We’ll run a controlled failover with two synthetic workloads and one production-simulated workload for the prioritized prefixes. Please confirm attendees from Silverline and the prioritized prefix list (CSV).

I’ll upload the runbook excerpt and the SLA draft to the shared Drive (link below). If that looks good, we can generate a redline-ready DocuSign package for the SLA appendix.
